title: DRAW???: One King Tempo Changes Everything
summary: Compare two nearly identical pawn endings: moving the king closer before liquidation changes a draw into a win.

nodes.question: Should White save the outside pawn or activate the king?
nodes.explanation: After the bishop and knight have been exchanged, White has Kf3/a5/h2 against Kb5/g5/h3. The extra king tempo is decisive.

nodes.question: What if White had liquidated with the king still on e2?
nodes.explanation: The same pawns and black king remain, but White’s king is one step farther from the kingside. The exact position is drawn.

branches.title: Independent legal reconstruction of the winning king race
commentary: After the bishop and knight have been exchanged, White has Kf3/a5/h2 against Kb5/g5/h3. The extra king tempo is decisive.
Kg4 approaches both kingside pawns. White allows a5 to fall because the king’s head start matters more than that pawn.
Kxa5 collects the outside pawn. This is an independently chosen representative reply, not a claim that every sampled king animation is a complete move.
Kxh3 must come first: this is the only winning move in this exact position. Taking g5 instead would give up the win.
Kb5 starts Black’s journey toward the drawing corner.
Kg4 returns toward g5 while keeping the winning tempo. This is the only win-preserving move in this exact position.
Kc5 continues toward the kingside. Black cannot repair the lost tempo in this selected line.
Kxg5 removes the last black pawn. White’s king is now on g5, rather than h3 as in the wrong capture order. The exact remaining rook-pawn ending is winning; the later conversion is not encoded here.

exercises.prompt: Why can White give up a5?
exercises.answer: Kf3 is close enough to collect the kingside pawns and win the remaining rook-pawn ending. The distant a-pawn buys time by drawing Black’s king away.

exercises.prompt: Why is the same material drawn with Ke2?
exercises.answer: White needs another king move before reaching the kingside. That lost tempo changes the exact result; the earlier king placement matters more than the material count.

startContext: The verified lesson begins in two six-piece diagrams after ...fxg5: White Kf3 at 108s versus White Ke2 at 87s. Both diagrams are reconstructed from saved images. All encoded race replies are independent legal representative continuations because the source’s sampled king-race animation skips moves. The earlier eight-piece Nd4/Kf3 zugzwang and its uniqueness claim remain unverified source context.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
